headline: Approved a request for a law department opinion on using AI to document meetings and prepare minutes.
summary: The meeting covered a welcome for new associate member Jaylynne Ogbeide and a discussion of the bylaws review. Trustees also talked about a City Council motion to allow patrons on the Bookmobile and heard the director's summer report. The only votes were to ask the law department for an opinion on AI meeting minutes and to accept the June 10 minutes.
decisions: Approved asking the law department for an opinion on AI-supported meeting minutes, by unanimous vote.
Approved the June 10, 2026 meeting minutes with no revisions, unanimously.

decision_titles: Request for law department opinion on AI-supported meeting minutes
plain_text:
Pollard Memorial Board of Trustees  – Trustee Minutes
Date:
o The meeting took place on Wednesday, September 9, 2026.
Location: 
o The meeting was held at Pollard Memorial Library (PML), 401 Merrimack St. Lowell, MA, as a 
hybrid meeting, both in person and via Zoom.
Opening Business
Meeting Call to Order
o The meeting was called to order by Donna Richards at 5:35 pm.
Attendance
Present: Excused: Guests:
Bridget Cooley, Library Director
     Donna Richards, Chair
     Ellen Anstey, Vice Chair
     Judith Davidson, Secretary
     Suzanne Frechette ZOOM
     Helen Littlefield
     Courtney McSparron
     Jack Moynihan
     Jaylynne Ogbeide ZOOM
     Christine O’Connor ZOOM
     Christopher St. Croix
Adoption of / Amendment to Agenda
o The agenda for September 9th was unanimously approved on a motion by Donna Richards, 
seconded by Jack Moynihan.
Prior Meeting Minutes Approval
o The meeting minutes from June 10, 2026 were unanimously accepted with no revisions on a 
motion by Ellen Anstey and seconded by Helen Littlefield.
o Chair Richards recommended attaching the packet prepared for the 4.21.26 City Council 
meeting be posted with the minutes of this meeting.  Director Cooley will do so.
Public Comment Period
o Public comment time was made available.  However, no members of the public were present 
to make a comment at this meeting.
2
Current Business
Welcome Associate Member Jaylynne Ogbeide
o Jaylynne Ogbeide was appointed by City Manager, Tom Golden, as an Associate Member of 
the PML Board of trustees.  The City Council approved her appointment (very enthusiastically) 
on September 8, 2026.  Ogbeide recently graduated from the business school of UMass 
Lowell.  She grew up in Lowell—living across from the library for many of those years—and 
using the library on a regular basis.
Could the Trustees use AI to document meetings and prepare formal meeting minutes?
o There was significant, extended discussion about this topic.  Top among the concerns raised 
were the issues about Freedom of Information Act requests.  Trustees agreed to hold off on 
making any changes until the legal questions are better clarified. O’Connor suggested that the 
Board of Trustees make a motion on this issue and request an opinion from the law 
department.  Richards makes a motion to have the law department provide us with an 
opinion on the use of AI supported meeting minutes.  Littlefield seconds.  Vote was 
unanimous in favor.  Richards will send letter to law office.
Review of PML Board of Trustees Bylaws
o Next steps in our process were reconfirmed:
 Chris O’Connor will review our by-law documents, make decisions about format and then 
return to trustees.  Once the trustees have approved the final document, we will forward 
to the Law Department for their review.
Update from Strategic Plan Task Groups:  No updates
o Culture (Judy Davidson / Courtney McSparron)
o Advocacy (Donna Richards / Ellen Anstey)
o City Engagement (Ellen Anstey / Donna Richards)
o Community Engagement (Courtney McSparron / Christine O’Connor)
o Planning & Building Usage-Accessibility (Helen Littlefield / Jack Moynihan)
o Collection Development (Library Staff Only)
Reports
Chairperson’s Report
o Mia Graceffa sent a heartfelt thank you on 7/27/26 for those who were able to volunteer at 
the Library table during the Folk Festival. This note is included below:
TO: TRUSTEES - Helen Littlefield, Jack Moynihan, Judy Davidson   FOUNDATION - Katy Aronoff, 
Linda Kilbride, Michael Breda
I just wanted to extend my gratitude to all of you for your help at Folk Fest over the weekend!
I don't know what we would have done without you all ... especially the Sunday crew who took
over after Bridget went home sick. By Sunday at 2pm, I got burnt out, and it was such a luxury 
to be able to sit back and play Mah Jong in my iPhone to recharge my batteries.
3
Special shout out to Michael Breda who basically morphed into Bridget and was the main 
evangelist for the library all day ... enthusiastically spreading that PML gospel. If there ever is 
an outreach team of library supporters, I vote Michael for president of it and Helen for VP. 
You all were such a huge help, even if you didn't feel like it. YOU WERE! Thank you.
It was also nice to sit and chat with you all. We should do it more!  Thanks again,  Mia
 A discussion followed the reading of the message from Graceffa.  A point made was that 
over the last few years, Trustees have interacted more with library staff than at earlier 
periods.  Staff recognize Trustees and visa-versa.  Trustee participation in this public event 
is an illustration of how this dynamic has changed. 
o Richards mentioned that a Motion to allow patrons on the Bookmobile was made at the 
9/8/26 City Council meeting by Vesna Nuon and Belinda Juran.  The motion by the councilors 
was made as a follow-up to a request from library staff member, Mia Graceffa.  The motion 
passed and a motion response will be requested from the interested departments.
 Points of information/issues raised in the Trustee’s discussion of the motion included the 
following: 
 The Book Mobile PML purchased was tested and measured to ensure it could 
be navigated on the very narrow old streets that still exist in Lowell 
neighborhoods.   The bookmobile was not designed to have people on board.
 Safety of patrons and staff.
 Appropriate liability insurance.
 Policies.
 Disability access.
o MLS Learning HUB - Massachusetts Library System's learning opportunities have migrated to 
the MLS Learning Hub. In the future, all MLS workshops, webinars, events, and other learning 
opportunities will only be available through the training calendar on the Learning Hub. PML 
trustees are encouraged to create an account in the Learning Hub. To create an account go to 
the Learning Hub Home Page, scroll down past the "Sign In" section, and click on "Create new 
account".  Questions about the Learning Hub or help creating an account, please 
contact learninghub@masslibsystem.org. 
o Massachusetts Library Association Annual Conference will be held April 27 – 28, 2027 at the 
Boston Marriott Newton.  There will be educational sessions, networking opportunities, and a 
Furniture and Design Showcase.
o The Massachusetts Library Trustees Association annual meeting will be held Saturday, 11/21 
meeting in Worcester from 9-2:00.  If you would like to attend, you will need to register.
4
Committee Reports
o The Committees as defined in the current version of the Trustee Bylaws will meet on an as 
needed basis.  Current trustee assignments are listed.  When a committee convenes trustees 
can volunteer to participate. No committee has met at this time.
 Governance/Policy Committee (J. Davidson*/S. Frechette/C. O’Connor)
 Art Committee ( __ */Ellen Anstey/Donna Richards)
 Security/Building/Grounds (Suzanne Frechette*/Helen Littlefield)
 Outreach (Donna Richards*/Judy Davidson/Helen Littlefield)
 Nominating/Personnel ( ___ */Donna Richards/Ellen Anstey)
Director’s Report
o Bridget Cooley prepared Director’s Reports for July and August, which were distributed to 
trustees via email prior to the meeting.  Specific discussion arose around numerous issues 
including:
 Over the summer, the library functioned very well and programs were well attended.
 One of the biggest concerns was that the library was down seven positions (Since that 
time some positions have been posted).  A number of changes, including cross training 
and other initiatives ensured that staff loss did not have a negative impact on patrons.
 Summer reading programs had excellent attendance.  There has been lots of good 
patron feedback.
 The city’s Sidewalk reconstruction project was a problem over the summer as the 
Merrimack Street library entrance was closed.
 Cooley does have concerns about some new building projects: boiler/capital projects 
grant. 
 The 2nd floor classroom spaces are working and being used.
 Staff are listening to patron requests and ideas.
 Partnerships and collaborations with other organizations were positive.
 The library is working hard on making collections more accessible.
 Patron numbers and check outs were steady; Hoopla and Libby circulation also 
increased.
Grants
o There were no grants to report on.
PML Foundation (Donna Richards)
o Donna Richards provided the following PML Foundation Report.
 The PMLF did not meet over the summer.
 The next regular PMLF meeting is scheduled for September 16, 2026 at 8:30am.
Friends of the PML (Helen Littlefield)
o Helen Littlefield provided the following Friends Liaison Report.
 The Friends held a meeting on August 1.  This was also their prebook sale mtg.
 The Fall book sale will be held on 11/14 from 9-12; 10/17 9-12 will be the only book drop.
5
 The Friends were able to send 35 boxes of unsold books to Better World Books; The 
money they receive from this partnership goes into a credit account that Graceffa uses for 
book clubs.
 The Friends purchased a new license for Chrome Books, and have introduced passes for 
Wolf Hollow and Whistler House. There will be a special museum pass activity at the 
circulation desk to increase interest and use of the passes.  
 The Friends’ next meeting is 10/3 at 9:30 am in the Library Director’s office.
Old Business
o Review of materials to onboard new members.  This could be done by an ad hoc committee.  
(Christopher St. Croix and Donna Richards). A goal will be to create a binder with updated 
relevant information.  Jaylynne can critique the effectiveness of materials.
 Chris O’Connor—suggests we check with the law department to request information they 
have already prepared that could be helpful to new board members.
o Suggestions/discussion arose regarding how best to promote the library.  These ideas can be 
forwarded to ad hoc advocacy committee.  (Courtney McSparron and ----------)
 How might we bring attention to the consequences of increased use (programs overbook, 
patrons waiting months for a new book)?  
 How can we make a case for what increased funding could do/bring to the library. Eg. 
offer more programming, increase materials, open weekend hours, have a social worker in
the library, etc.  Compare services offered to other libraries to see what we are lacking.  
Compare # staff/ per person and $/ per person.  Highlight partnerships formed and value 
added.
 Identify and share the PML’s value to different areas of city operation.  For instance: How 
is the library part of public safety?  How do we contribute?  How do we amplify the goals 
of the city?  Can we quantify…how many people are not on the street because of the 
library?  What’s the impact when the library is closed?  [For holidays]  What different 
services are offered at the library and nowhere else ?
New Business (Announcements and Questions )
o Richards proposes we invite the three Lowell District STATE representatives and the Lowell 
District STATE senator to meet the trustees after the November elections to hear short 
presentations of library issues and where advocacy is needed.  This year we will elect two new
State Representatives and one new State Senator.  We will have only one incumbent. Our goal
is for local elected officials to understand how vastly different PML is from the other libraries 
in their regions.  O’Connor thinks a November meeting would be timely, but we should begin 
to plan the meeting in October.
o It was confirmed that our 11/11 meeting has been changed to 11/4; change due to Veteran’s 
Day Holiday on 11/11/26.
6
Adjournment
o The meeting was adjourned at 6:56 PM on a motion by Donna Richards and seconded by Jack 
Moynhihan.   All in attendance were in favor.
o Our next meeting is October 14, 2026.  5:30 pm.
APPROVED: 10/14/2026  Pollard Library Board of trustees
